name: Shuffle-TS-TW
title: Shuffle
description: The letters of a single word are split into vertical strips and rolled upward into their final shapes, so the word clicks into place a character at a time. Hovering replays the roll.
use: A single display word should arrive with a mechanical roll when seen or hovered.
avoid: Long lines or body text: the per-letter roll needs a short word to read.
a11y: Replay is hover-only, so keyboard users cannot retrigger it; reduced motion is respected. (keyboard: no, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: The word "SHUFFLE" runs across a black stage in wide-tracked, thin white capitals. Letterforms are simple and evenly spaced with plenty of air around them.
behaves: On entering view each letter rolls vertically through a stack of copies before landing on the real glyph, staggered so the word assembles left to right. Hovering the word runs the roll again.
customise: The text, tag, direction, duration, easing, stagger, roll count, hover trigger, loop and colour range are props.
weight: light: One short timeline on per-character strips; idle once it settles.
issues: Mid-roll frames show chopped glyph fragments that read as broken type out of context.
polishWhy: Crisp wide tracking and a tidy roll; the split frames can look like broken type.
